title: Support multiple player characters
description: Design and implement support for campaigns with multiple player characters instead of assuming a single protagonist. Scope includes character identity, turn/input attribution, party state, scene context, memory summaries, CLI/player UX, and persistence/query changes needed for solo multi-PC or small-group play.
design: Initial epic only. Design work should establish: (1) whether multiple PCs are controlled by one local user, multiple human players, or both; (2) how player input is attributed to a PC or party; (3) how existing character/state tables and mutations represent multiple PCs; (4) how context assembly and memory summaries preserve individual character perspective and party canon; (5) CLI affordances for creating/selecting/switching active PC; (6) migration/backward compatibility for existing single-PC campaign DBs.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed design exists before implementation tasks are created; implementation supports at least two player characters in one campaign; deterministic state mutations can target each PC independently; context assembly includes relevant party and active-PC state; session summaries preserve per-PC important facts; existing single-PC flows keep working or have a documented migration path; tests cover persistence, state mutation, context assembly, and CLI flow for multi-PC campaigns.
notes: Design drafted at docs/multi-pc-design.md (branch work/loreweaver-d4d). Foundation (v9) needs no further migration; remaining work is a read/orchestration/UX layer. Proposed 7-issue breakdown awaits review before child issues are created.
close_reason: All 7 child issues complete. Multi-PC support delivered: party roster reads, party-aware context assembly + owner-scoped inventory, per-tool character targeting, acting-character attribution, CLI party UX (/party,/switch,/addpc), per-PC scene salient refs (schema v9->v10), and docs. Design at docs/multi-pc-design.md. PR #100.
